name: PA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 8 points on the PVI
Incumbent Madeleine Dean has a large fundraising edge and $1.2M on hand
Prediction markets price Dean near 94% to win
No public polls or expert ratings, so uncertainty stays wide
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Dean: a Democratic-leaning suburban Philadelphia seat, incumbency, and a decisive money advantage over challenger Aurora Stuski, with markets pricing her near-certain to win. With no polls to sharpen the picture, the margin stays at the fundamentals level of roughly 20 points.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Dean or an unusually strong Republican wave environment could pull the margin closer to single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Madeleine Dean seeks another term in a Democratic-leaning suburban Philadelphia district that favored her party by about eight points at the baseline. She has raised $1.37 million and holds $1.18 million on hand, while Republican challenger Aurora Stuski shows no reported fundraising and no outside support on either side. Prediction markets give Dean roughly a 94 percent chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those all point the same way, though the absence of polling keeps the uncertainty band wide. Dean remains the clear favorite, with the main risk being a national environment that breaks sharply against her party.
